webmFallback.note: Isolated video-element tests against Cloudinary renditions. These validate media support; they are not full-site integration tests.
findings: LT Browser 107 plays and seeks the VP9 WebM testimonial rendition at 1280x720 and 720x404.
The Cloudinary hero WebM with q_auto:best,ki_1,f_webm fails with MEDIA_ELEMENT_ERROR: Format error in Chrome too.
The Cloudinary hero WebM without ki_1 loads but exposes no finite duration in Chrome, so the hero scroll mapping cannot use it as a drop-in fallback.
A production hero fallback needs a validated WebM/VP9 rendition with finite duration, cues, and seek support.

confirmed: LT Browser 107 reports no H.264/AVC1 support: canPlayType("video/mp4; codecs=avc1.42E01E") is empty and MediaCapabilities supported is false.
Both the hero and testimonial MP4 elements fail with MediaError code 4 (MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED), readyState 0, networkState 3, duration null, videoWidth/videoHeight 0.
The MP4 requests return HTTP 206 with video/mp4; the network path is not the blocker. The same URLs work in Chrome 156.
The hero failure happens before seeking: there are no seeking/seeked events, currentTime stays 0, and video.seeking stays false. The serialized seek queue is not stuck in this failure.
The testimonial failure is not an autoplay-policy or user-gesture issue: play() rejects with NotSupportedError "The element has no supported sources." even with autoplay explicitly allowed.
The video elements are mounted, visible, opacity 1, and have nonzero layout boxes. CSS, sticky positioning, and section layering are not hiding them.
In Chrome 156, the hero seeks to 4.98s at 50% and 9.96s at 100%; the testimonial plays and advances. The same production build works in the control browser.
Story frames still load and the visible frame advances in LT Browser, but img.decode() is much slower: median 227ms at 1792x1120 and 309ms at 360x640/DPR3, versus 10.6ms and 9.6ms in Chrome.
hypotheses: The Story lag is primarily decode cost in the old LT Browser Chromium build; frame request timing was noisy and not consistently worse than Chrome.
The 300ms DECODE_FALLBACK_MS is close to the LT Browser median decode time and may fire before decode completes on the mobile profile. This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed cause of the visible lag.
LT Browser headless may use a slower software decode path than its normal window, so the absolute Story decode times may be pessimistic; the H.264 capability gap is independent of headless mode.
unknowns: The physical 16-inch MacBook Pro and Galaxy J7 Max were not tested; all device-profile results are emulation results.
The normal LT Browser UI could not be fully automated through CDP in this pass; the installed build was tested headless. The user report supplies the UI-level reproduction.
The exact GPU/decode path used by LT Browser in normal windowed mode is unknown.
No validated hero WebM fallback was found among the Cloudinary transformations tested.

recommendations.hero: Do not add a naive Cloudinary f_webm fallback. Either require an H.264-capable browser or supply a validated WebM/VP9 rendition with finite duration, cues, and byte-range seeking, then retest the scroll mapping. The existing seek queue does not need a change for this failure.
recommendations.testimonials: Smallest product fix if LT Browser support is required: use <source> elements with the existing MP4 first and the verified VP9 WebM rendition second. Keep the MP4 for browsers with H.264. This was verified in isolation at both 1280x720 and 720x404, but not integrated into the site in this pass.
recommendations.story: No frame-pipeline change is justified by LT Browser alone. If the lag reproduces on a real target device, investigate smaller frame renditions or a decode budget while preserving the 56-frame order, mapping, and section height. Do not change DECODE_FALLBACK_MS without a controlled A/B test.
recommendations.queue: Residual risk only: a future failure that leaves video.seeking=true with no seeked event would stall the queue. No evidence of that occurred here; add a timeout/retry only if reproduced.

limitations: LT Browser 107 headless was used for automation; this is not a physical-device test.
The 1080x1920 Galaxy J7 Max profile was tested both as a raw CSS viewport and as 360x640 CSS at DPR 3; the exact LT Browser profile mapping is not exposed by the app.
Cold-cache runs and localhost preview conditions are not identical to a user network.
The WebM fallback tests used isolated video elements, not the integrated site.
